quotes.text: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is developing faster than our laws can keep up—and Congress is failing the American people by letting it happen.

Innovation and remaining competitive at the global stage cannot come at the expense of the American people. In fact, the U.S. and China should consider a treaty to slow down the AI race before it's too late.

Called for an AI Treaty. As AI rapidly advances in the U.S. and around the globe, the Trump administration must immediately initiate dialogue with allies, and also competitors and adversaries, to engage in comprehensive and urgent negotiations regarding the future of AI.
It is time for Congress to put people before profits and establish strong, smart, enforceable rules without sacrificing our ability to be a global leader in AI.

Unfortunately, we have the dubious distinction of breaking heat records in my community now, and we have three data centers going up in our region already, with another one planned on our military installation. And these data centers are using gas turbines to more than double the electrical output.

One of the things we're working with them is to shorten the kill chains. We're doing a lot of stuff with artificial intelligence and machine learning to be able to do dynamic targeting. But we are seeing, and our goal is by this January from a year ago, to be able to increase 700 percent our ability to target dynamic targets in a 24-hour period.

We mentioned artificial intelligence. We mentioned robotics, precision munitions, the ability to sense the distances that have never been before done in human history. All of these things in combination are going to fundamentally change in my view the very character of war probably inside of a decade, for sure inside of 15 years. [...] And the country that optimizes those technologies for the conduct of war are likely to have decisive advantage. And that country needs to be us. So I would strongly recommend that we execute all those innovative technologies.
